notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/testimonialscard.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/testimonialscard.md at e7ed622 (“docs: publish 19 Component Fix fixes on jfs-components dbe0e02”, 28 October), the same files on main and docs-next (the guide was added at ccb4c4c on 26 October; nothing changed them after e7ed622). The guide's Sources note was checked on 28 October 2026 on what it calls the 27 October build of Biscuit's main, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02, which is the installed build, so items citing it carry 2026-10-28 and 0.1.78-dbe0e02. The evidence's “dbe0e02 publish (28 October 2026, #406)” section replaces its older 26 October sections (on c8526ae) wherever they disagree, so the superseded points are not cited: the crossed text colours, the 17 px name line, the 4 px gap and 117 px card, monogram needing style Monogram, the sample photo without avatarProps, avatarProps.modes replacing the card's modes, and no pressed or disabled look. Evidence items cite the dbe0e02 section with its own date and build (2026-10-28, 0.1.78-dbe0e02); the only older line cited is the 26 October Sources section's summary of Biscuit's handwritten TestimonialsCard.mdx, for avoidWhen (2026-10-26, 0.1.78-c8526ae): the .mdx is not in the mirror (src/components/TestimonialsCard holds only TestimonialsCard.tsx at both v0.1.78-c8526ae and v0.1.78-dbe0e02), so it could not be re-read on dbe0e02; the dbe0e02 section doesn't contradict it, and the installed props have no rating, date or link either. Read against the installed TestimonialsCard.tsx (not rendered), with token values through the package's own getVariableByName (lib/commonjs): the card is a column 180 px wide, hard-coded (line 136), with alignItems flex-start (141), testimonialsCard/gap 12, padding 12 on every side, radius 8 and a white background; the 1 px rgb(232,232,232) border is an absolute overlay, so it adds no size (145–162). The name is 14 px, weight 700, on a 16 px line (testimonialsCard/title/lineHeight doesn't exist, so it falls back to testimonialsCard/subtitle/lineHeight, 16; lines 115–123), 2 px (title/gap in context7 Card, 103–104) above the quote, 12 px, weight 400, on a 16 px line (126–132), both rgb(13,13,15). So 12 + 42 + 12 + 16 + 2 + 16 + 12 = 112 for a one-line quote, and each further line adds 16; the body has no line clamp. The Avatar is always rendered, inside a view hidden from screen readers (215–227); its style is avatarProps.style, else Monogram when monogram is set or there is no imageSource, else Image (195–196); its monogram is avatarProps.monogram, else the first letters of the title's first two words (21–27, 197–199), so “Aarav S.” gives AS; its modes are the card's modes with avatarProps.modes on top (190–193). Avatar Size L, M, S and XS resolve avatar/size to 42, 36, 29 and 14 px, L is the default, and the card's own tokens don't change with it. An empty title or body hides its line (229, 239). Without onPress the card is a View carrying the label: on the web role group with aria-label, natively accessible with accessibilityRole text (282–293); the label is accessibilityLabel, else “Testimonial from {title}: {body}” (201–202), and the texts are hidden, so it reads once. With onPress it is a Pressable with role button and that label, dimmed to 0.7 while pressed unless disabled (258–279), with no hover style. disabled applies only with onPress: opacity 0.5, the Pressable disabled and aria-disabled on the web (143, 253–256, 270–274); without onPress it changes nothing (the dbe0e02 evidence: “Disabled without onPress leaves a static card alone”). Every guide sentence used here matches the installed build; none is contradicted, so no human flag. Two read with care: States' “Without onPress the card is text” is accessibilityRole text natively and a named group on the web; either way the card is read once, so it is quoted. States' “disabled dims it to half, stops presses, and takes it out of the Tab order.” holds only with onPress (the guide's own disabled card sets both): it is quoted, and the configuration rule from the disabled fact adds the condition. Open ticket #418 (Component Bug, Component Fix In progress, Mr. Biscuit): every render logs the console warning “Variable with name "testimonialsCard/title/lineHeight" not found” (it shows here too when the tokens are resolved); the layout is right (16 px name line, 112 px card). It is a developer console warning, not a usage gap, so it is in no rule and no gap. useWhen: the summary and the core principle. avoidWhen: the guide names no case, so the three items come from the evidence's summary of Biscuit's .mdx (not a review with stars or a profile; no rating, date, or link), as SummaryTile's and CardFeedback's do. ProfileCard has an entry, so that rule carries useInstead; Rating is not a jfs-components export (the package has CircularRating, which the .mdx doesn't name), so the stars rule has none. The Don'ts “The brand’s initials” and “A paragraph of marketing” are content guidance, so they are content rules, not avoidWhen. Anatomy: Avatar and Card are always present; Name and Quote are not marked always present: title and body are optional props, and although the package renders them by default (“Title” and its sample quote), an empty string hides each line (TestimonialsCard.tsx 229, 239). Modes: Avatar Size is the only collection the guide describes, and no guide sentence says when to pick M or S, so the configuration items say what it does and no rule asks for one; XS (14 px) is in the facts, but the guide names three sizes. The other collections in the facts (Badge Size, context 10, Context2, Context4, Page type, Profile Card Appearance) come from the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES and the guide says nothing about them. Content: good keeps the guide's names and quotes; bad keeps the two Don't specimens, the brand's initials “JF” and the marketing paragraph. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every component), no Slot gap modes, no style (paddingVertical 16, width 100% and paddingHorizontal 12 are the docs frame). The In context example is the guide's row: a VStack holding a Title and a horizontal ScrollArea › HStack of four cards, each with onPress (the empty handler stands for opening that customer's review) and an accessibilityLabel that says where it goes; ScrollArea has no entry in this pack and is used only as the guide does, as the horizontal scroller its In context needs (“the row scrolls instead of squeezing them”); Title, VStack and HStack have entries; alignVertical flex-start is kept as the guide writes it (it is HStack's default cross-axis alignment, stackAlignment.ts). The cards pass avatarProps={{ monogram }} alone, which the Sources note says shows initials on this build, instead of the guide's MONO helper (style Monogram plus monogram). The second example is a single quote with no onPress and no avatarProps, so its initials come from the title (Configuration). The third shows a photo through avatarProps.imageSource; the URI stands for the person's own photo. Not recorded: style (the building rules keep style overrides off Coin components); Color Mode and dark mode; Figma's hex values; the Storybook story list; the playground and its Readout (“onPress makes the whole card one button, which dims while pressed.” is playground copy, not a section); “Shown at 1.5×”. Gaps: the Sources note's Figma difference (Figma's Title, Body, Show Footer Text and Show Button properties change no layer). Sorting (batch 12, rounds 1 and 2): two cross-check runs. Round 1 raised four flags, all our extraction's wording, none about the installed build: /configuration/5 and /placementAdvice/0 generalised the guide's one In context row (each card opening a review through onPress; the row under a section title), so both now say they describe the guide's In context, and the onPress item says onPress is optional; /anatomy/1 and /anatomy/2 marked Name and Quote always present, but title and body are optional and an empty string hides each line (the older evidence's “Empty hides it.” still holds on dbe0e02, lines 229 and 239), so both are now not required. Round 2 ran on that final entry and raised no flags. Its notes, not flags: /examples/0's HStack alignVertical, Title's title and subtitle and ScrollArea direction horizontal are the guide's own code (testimonialscard.guide.tsx lines 88–90), which the reviewer doesn't see; the guide's ScreenFrame is the docs site's phone frame (guide-kit), not a jfs-components export, so the example leaves it out. Round 1 also noted that the evidence's Limits paragraph (“Don't imply … a pressed or disabled look … or that `monogram` alone shows initials”) is stale after the #406 fixes; nothing here cites it, and it is reported to the coordinator as an evidence fix. No dismissals, no human flag; no trace-check flags remain.

examples.purpose: A row of quotes, the guide's In context: a Title over a row that scrolls sideways, each card keeping its 180 px. Each card shows the customer's initials through avatarProps' monogram, opens that customer's full review through onPress (the empty handler stands for opening it), and has an accessibilityLabel that says where it goes. ScrollArea has no entry in this pack; it is the horizontal scroller the guide's In context uses.

  <ScrollArea direction="horizontal">
    <HStack alignVertical="flex-start">
      <TestimonialsCard
        title="Aarav S."
        body="Renewing my car insurance took a minute."
        avatarProps={{ monogram: 'AS' }}
        onPress={() => {}}
        accessibilityLabel="Read Aarav S.’s full review"
      />
      <TestimonialsCard
        title="Priya M."
        body="Simple, fast, reliable."
        avatarProps={{ monogram: 'PM' }}
        onPress={() => {}}
        accessibilityLabel="Read Priya M.’s full review"
      />
      <TestimonialsCard
        title="Rohan K."
        body="Setting up my first SIP took less than two minutes."
        avatarProps={{ monogram: 'RK' }}
        onPress={() => {}}
        accessibilityLabel="Read Rohan K.’s full review"
      />
      <TestimonialsCard
        title="Neha J."
        body="I see all my accounts and my gold in one place now."
        avatarProps={{ monogram: 'NJ' }}
        onPress={() => {}}
        accessibilityLabel="Read Neha J.’s full review"
      />
    </HStack>
  </ScrollArea>
</VStack>
